acceptance_met: Metadata advertises N live nodes plus dead ids with configurable per-partition leadership (explicit map or round-robin over live nodes); one node can delay every response by a fixed duration (--nodes/--dead-nodes/--slow-node/--slow-delay-ms).

Seeded injection of NOT_LEADER_OR_FOLLOWER on Produce/Fetch follows --fault-seed/--fault-rate-per-million (splitmix64 over a per-request counter, deterministic per seed), fails fast before append so retries stay exact, and is counted server-side as injected_errors; wrong-node requests return 6 and count as leader_mismatches.

All modes default off (1 node, no slow, 0 ppm) and are recorded in every artifact under modes{} alongside injected_errors/leader_mismatches; nullbroker stays workspace-excluded with zero dependencies.
commands: cargo test --locked --manifest-path benchmarks/nullbroker/Cargo.toml (19 unit + 7 interop passed; interop suite 10/10 repeat runs green)

3-node validation: nullbroker --nodes 3 --slow-node 2 --slow-delay-ms 2 --fault-seed 20260926 --fault-rate-per-million 10000 + bench_produce COUNT=20000 LINGER_MS=0: client acked 20000, server accepted 20000, 62 injected (~1.05% of 5905 requests), zero validation failures, zero leader mismatches
limits: Dead ids advertise computed ports with no listener (connection refused); the suite asserts the dead port differs from live ports rather than asserting refusal, since a parallel test may hold any ephemeral port.
Slow-node delay applies per response after handling; isolation of slow partitions from fast ones is client scheduling, not broker-enforced.
Fault decisions are per request (all partitions in an injected request fail); acks=0 never faults to avoid invisible loss.
